role: faithful implementation of the charter's already-frozen aggregation_contract; this gate does NOT redesign it

charter_clause_transcribed.single_source: every timeframe is built from the SAME 1m atoms. A coarse bar is never taken from a vendor endpoint while its finer bars come from another — that is how two timeframes silently disagree.
charter_clause_transcribed.boundary_convention: left-closed, left-labelled: a bar stamped 09:30 covers [09:30, 09:45) for 15m. Stated because it is the single most common silent mismatch between two pipelines.

session_aligned_1H.rule: 1H bars are aligned to the SESSION, not to the wall clock: 09:30-10:30, 10:30-11:30, ... , 15:30-16:00
session_aligned_1H.why: clock-aligned hours would split the opening 30 minutes into a stub bar and make the first hour non-comparable across days
session_aligned_1H.last_bar: the final session hour is a 30-minute stub and must be FLAGGED as short, never silently treated as a full hour

vwap_rule.correct: recompute as sum(vw_i * v_i) / sum(v_i) over the constituent 1m bars
vwap_rule.incorrect: mean(vw_i) — an unweighted average of VWAPs is not a VWAP
vwap_rule.zero_volume: a window whose total volume is 0 has UNDEFINED vwap; it is recorded as null, never as 0 and never forward-filled

sparse_minutes.expectation: minutes with no trades are OMITTED by the vendor, so a 1m series is NOT a dense grid
sparse_minutes.volume_rule: an absent minute means ZERO volume, not missing volume
sparse_minutes.price_rule: an absent minute has NO price. It is not forward-filled in the stored atoms. Any feature needing a continuous price must declare its own fill rule in the feature dictionary.
sparse_minutes.why_it_matters: slot-RVOL and CUM-RVOL divide by a per-slot baseline. If absent minutes are dropped instead of counted as zero, the baseline is computed over a biased subset of days and every RVOL is inflated for illiquid names.

adjustment.issue: split/dividend adjustment is DECISION-CRITICAL over a multi-year 1m history: an unadjusted series has discontinuities at every split, and an adjusted one may be restated retroactively by the vendor
adjustment.requirement: the programme must choose ONE regime, seal it, and record the vendor's adjustment behaviour. Mixing adjusted coarse bars with unadjusted atoms is a defect, not a nuance.

timeframe_registry.rule: an additional timeframe is search-space expansion and requires a separate pre-Y amendment
timeframe_registry.single_source: every timeframe is built from the SAME 1m atoms. A coarse bar is never taken from a vendor endpoint while its finer bars come from another — that is how two timeframes silently disagree.

one_minute_role_preserved.invariant: 1m is a measurement / clock layer; a 1m-derived quantity must name the coarser or session-level parent it measures
forbidden: searching for thresholds, patterns or rules AT 1m granularity
promoting any 1m-native construct to a signal
using 1m to redefine a coarse-TF state after seeing outcomes
one_minute_role_preserved.why_this_gate_exists: to give EMA a legitimate coarse-TF parent rather than amending the constraint away

interval_alignment.convention: left-closed, left-labelled: a bar stamped 09:30 covers [09:30, 09:45) for 15m. Stated because it is the single most common silent mismatch between two pipelines.
interval_alignment.measured_note: both 390 and 210 divide evenly by 15, so 15m NEVER produces a stub. 1H produces exactly one 30-minute stub in BOTH cases — confirming the charter's stub applies to early closes too, not only to normal sessions.
interval_alignment.derived_from: the XNYS calendar, not from assumed clock times

hour_stub.rule: 1H bars are aligned to the SESSION, not to the wall clock: 09:30-10:30, 10:30-11:30, ... , 15:30-16:00
hour_stub.why: clock-aligned hours would split the opening 30 minutes into a stub bar and make the first hour non-comparable across days
hour_stub.last_bar: the final session hour is a 30-minute stub and must be FLAGGED as short, never silently treated as a full hour
forbidden: mixing it with the session-close-boundary bar

input_scope.permitted: regular-session observed 1m bars from the production V1 derived base

unobserved_propagation.inherited_rule: a coarser bar (15m/1H/1D) whose window contains ANY UNOBSERVED minute is flagged UNOBSERVED_CONTAMINATED and carries the count of such minutes
unobserved_propagation.forbidden: silently computing an inferentially valid coarse bar from the remaining observed subset

measured_contamination.headline: under the strict any-UNOBSERVED rule roughly TWO THIRDS of daily bars are contaminated
measured_contamination.arithmetic: 7.6% of expected minutes are UNOBSERVED, and a daily interval has 390 chances to contain one
measured_contamination.not_a_defect: this is the inherited arithmetic of honest 1m accounting, not an aggregation error
measured_contamination.consequence_for_ema: an EMA over daily bars where only 36.3% are COMPLETE would either reset almost continuously or would have to consume contaminated bars
measured_contamination.why_not: the charter says a contaminated bar 'is not silently dropped and not silently used; each study declares its own tolerance, and the declaration is part of that study's specification'. Setting one here would make that declaration for a study that does not exist yet.
measured_contamination.why_measured_now: so the tolerance is declared by someone who knows it is 63.7% at 1D and not 5% — while Y_EXPOSED is still 0

observed_zero_vs_unobserved.observed_zero: an archived 1m vendor bar with volume 0 is an OBSERVED input
observed_zero_vs_unobserved.unobserved: no source bar for an expected minute

coarse_ohlcv.forbidden: using this formula to disguise missing expected input

vwap.reason: carried from Builder Spec V2 — vendor vw may lie outside [low, high]; true VWAP cannot be reconstructed from OHLCV
vwap.charter_recompute_rule: recompute as sum(vw_i * v_i) / sum(v_i) over the constituent 1m bars
vwap.note: the charter's recompute rule is transcribed for provenance but the feature stays disabled in this programme

causal_availability.rule: a coarse bar becomes available only after its final required constituent minute completes
causal_availability.example: a 15m bar cannot affect state at one of its own earlier constituent 1m minutes
causal_availability.inheritance: any later EMA or other feature based on that coarse bar inherits this availability timestamp

coarse_feature_eligibility.rule: future EMA may consume only coarse observations satisfying the frozen complete-input contract

required: pre-market minute cannot enter a coarse regular bar
close-boundary bar cannot enter a coarse regular bar
post-market minute cannot enter a coarse regular bar
UNOBSERVED minute cannot become volume zero
UNOBSERVED-contaminated interval cannot be marked COMPLETE
a 15m bar cannot become available before its closing constituent minute
the 1H final 30-minute stub cannot be padded to 60 minutes
an early-close session cannot generate nonexistent later coarse bars
aggregation cannot cross an XNYS session boundary
a supplemental row cannot enter aggregation
an excluded security cannot enter output
negative_fixtures.standard: each must show the dangerous version FAILS and the correct version PASSES

forward_risk.flagged: the 1D COMPLETE share is 36.3%. Any downstream contract that requires strictly COMPLETE daily bars for a long-period EMA should expect heavy fragmentation.
forward_risk.decision_belongs_to: the EMA/RVOL spec reissue, which must declare its contamination tolerance explicitly and before Y

next_step: coarse aggregation smoke + label-free capability. Full coarse production is NOT built automatically.
